old.body_zh: 展厅里的纸本作品通常采用较低的照明强度，因为长时间的强光会让纸张发黄，颜料褪色，许多美术馆把这类展品的照度控制在50勒克斯左右，并定期轮换展出，原作收回库房期间，墙上会换上同样尺寸的复制品。
old.body_en: Works on paper are usually shown under low light, because long exposure to strong light yellows the paper and fades the pigments. Many museums keep the light level for such pieces at around 50 lux and rotate them on and off display. While an original is back in storage, a reproduction of the same size hangs in its place.

new_zh: 油画在展厅墙面上悬挂时，画面中心通常位于离地约150厘米的高度，这个高度接近成年观众平视的视线。相邻两幅作品之间一般留出不少于60厘米的空隙，尺寸较大的作品前方还会留出更宽的观看距离，以免观众挤在一处。
new_en: When oil paintings are hung on gallery walls, the center of each picture is usually placed about 150 centimeters above the floor, close to the eye level of an adult visitor. Neighboring works are normally spaced at least 60 centimeters apart, and larger works are given a wider viewing distance in front, so that visitors do not crowd into one spot.
